findings.description: This subnet automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses and is associated with a route table whose default route leads to an internet gateway. Workloads launched here can be internet-reachable when their security groups permit it.

This subnet automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses and is associated with a route table whose default route leads to an internet gateway. The portal instance is launched here and is publicly reachable through its attached security group.
The separately attached EBS volume does not explicitly enable encryption. Its data is not guaranteed to be encrypted at rest by this configuration.

The user-data script contains an AWS access key ID and secret access key. The credentials can be exposed through source control, Terraform state, or instance/user-data access and used with the associated IAM principal's permissions.
No root block device encryption is explicitly configured for the instance's root EBS volume. Encryption at rest for the operating-system disk is therefore not guaranteed by this configuration.
TCP/22 is permitted from 0.0.0.0/0. Attached to an instance with a public IP in an internet-routable subnet, this exposes SSH to arbitrary internet hosts.

TCP/80 is exposed to 0.0.0.0/0 on the publicly reachable instance, and the configuration provides no TLS listener or TLS-terminating endpoint. Web traffic to the service can therefore be transmitted in cleartext.

All protocols and ports are allowed to 0.0.0.0/0. This removes egress controls from the internet-facing instance, facilitating unrestricted command-and-control traffic or data exfiltration after compromise.
The S3 bucket receiving VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration. Encryption at rest for this network telemetry is not guaranteed by the Terraform configuration.
